entities.definition: A tiered storage architecture exploiting temporal and spatial locality where faster, smaller storage devices act as caches for larger, slower devices.
keyClaims: Organizes registers, SRAM cache, DRAM main memory, and disk in order of decreasing speed and increasing capacity
Exploits temporal and spatial locality in computer programs

entities.definition: Fast SRAM-based storage hardware situated between CPU registers and main memory to accelerate data access.
keyClaims: Organized into sets, lines, tags, and block offsets
Reduces average memory access latency by servicing CPU read and write requests from fast SRAM
Classified into direct-mapped, set-associative, and fully-associative caches

entities.definition: An operating system and hardware abstraction that provides each process with a private, uniform address space and manages physical memory allocation.
keyClaims: Treats main memory as a cache for disk-backed virtual address pages
Provides memory protection and process isolation
Simplifies linking and loading by providing a uniform address space

entities.definition: An in-memory data structure mapping virtual page numbers (VPN) to physical page numbers (PPN) with protection flags.
keyClaims: Maps virtual page numbers to physical page numbers or disk addresses
Uses multi-level hierarchical structures to minimize page table memory overhead
Triggers page faults when requested virtual pages are unmapped or invalid

entities.definition: A small, highly associative hardware cache inside the MMU that caches recent virtual-to-physical address translations.
keyClaims: Caches page table entries in hardware MMU
Eliminates memory lookup overhead during address translation on hits
Directly speeds up page translation for virtual memory

entities.definition: Hardware and OS mechanisms for abrupt control transfers in response to system events, classified into interrupts, traps, faults, and aborts.
keyClaims: Categorized into interrupts, traps, faults, and aborts
Traps provide intentional synchronous interface for user programs to invoke kernel system calls
Faults handle recoverable exceptional conditions like page faults

entities.definition: Distinct abstractions of execution contexts: processes own private virtual memory address spaces while threads share address spaces within a process.
keyClaims: Processes have separate private virtual memory address spaces and isolated resources
Threads share the same virtual address space, code segment, and global data while keeping private stacks and registers
Thread switching incurs lower context switch overhead than process switching

entities.definition: Architectures and OS primitives for handling multiple concurrent network socket connections, using processes, threads, or event-driven I/O multiplexing.
keyClaims: Employs process-based, thread-based, or non-blocking I/O multiplexing models
I/O multiplexing uses epoll/select to serve multiple connections on a single thread
Enables scalable concurrent network services without unbounded thread creation
